SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 27
NATURAL MINOR DIATONIC THIRDS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
======================================================================================================================================================

PURPOSE
Level 27 leaves stepwise and rolling natural-minor motion and begins intervallic sequencing.
Each pair skips one scale degree: 1-b3, 2-4, b3-5, and onward. After each upper note,
the next pair rolls back one degree and continues upward. The exercise retains the same
two-octave six-string natural-minor shape and one-fret chromatic neck route used in Levels
22, 24, and 26.

WHAT CHANGES FROM LEVEL 26
Level 26 moved in overlapping four-note scale fragments. Level 27 replaces those fragments
with two-note diatonic thirds. The mechanical demand is shorter, but the musical demand is
higher: hear whether each pair is a minor third or major third, preserve the one-degree
rollback, and keep every string crossing inside one uninterrupted line.

NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
One octave: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Two octaves: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8 9 b10 11 12 b13 b14 15
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole, then repeat

MAIN SEQUENCE
Ascending:  1-b3 | 2-4 | b3-5 | 4-b6 | 5-b7 | b6-8 | b7-9 | 8-b10 | 9-11 | b10-12 | 11-b13 | 12-b14 | b13-15
Descending: 15-b13 | b14-12 | b13-11 | 12-b10 | 11-9 | b10-8 | 9-b7 | 8-b6 | b7-5 | b6-4 | 5-b3 | 4-2 | b3-1
Each new pair begins one scale position farther forward. Between pairs, the line rolls back
one degree: 1-b3 then 2-4; 4-b6 then 5-b7. Do not pause or reset at the rollback.

INTERVAL-QUALITY PATTERN
Ascending:  m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3
Descending: M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3
M3 = major third = 4 semitones. m3 = minor third = 3 semitones.
First-octave natural-minor pattern: m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3.
Natural minor uses the same two third sizes as major, but the order begins differently.

TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4        Positions 1,2,b3
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4        Positions 4,5,b6
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3          Positions b7,8
G string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4        Positions 9,b10,11
B string:     R, R+1, R+3          Fingers 1,2,4        Positions 12,b13,b14
High e:       R                    Finger 1             Position 15
The complete map spans R-1 through R+3. Release and rebuild for the G-string backreach and
again for the B-string offset; do not hold a static five-fret stretch.

STRING-PATH MAP
Ascending:  EE | EA | EA | AA | AD | AD | DG | DG | GG | GB | GB | BB | Be
Descending: eB | BB | BG | BG | GG | GD | GD | DA | DA | AA | AE | AE | EE
Some thirds stay on one string; others cross one string boundary. Keep every landing equal
in volume and preserve the two-note pulse through the D-G and G-B transitions.

CELL DESIGN
- 13 ascending pairs / 26 notes
- repeat the high root at the turnaround
- 13 descending pairs / 26 notes
- 52 notes total per key
- shift the entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret only after the final b3-1 pair

PICKING
Downstroke start: D-U | D-U | D-U | ... through all 26 pairs.
Upstroke start:   U-D | U-D | U-D | ... through all 26 pairs.
Because each pair and the complete 52-note cell are even, every pair and every new key begins
with the same pick orientation. Do not reset at a string crossing, the middle octave, the
repeated high root, or a new key.

RHYTHM
Learning pulse: one pair per beat as eighth notes.
Performance pulse: two pairs per beat as straight sixteenth notes.
Accent the first note of each pair while learning, then remove the accents and equalize all notes.

PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. A natural minor, first octave only: pairs 1-b3 through b6-8, then reverse.
2. A natural minor, all 13 ascending pairs.
3. A natural minor, all 13 descending pairs.
4. Link the 52-note cell; articulate both high-root notes without resetting.
5. Use two or three neighboring keys with a one-beat pause only after each complete cell.
6. Remove the pause and complete the entire route with both pick starts.

CHROMATIC ROUTE
Up:   A -> Bb -> B -> C -> C# -> D -> Eb -> E -> F -> F# -> G -> G# -> A
Down: G# -> G -> F# -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> C# -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-natural-minor rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.

03    B natural minor              fret 7        6-10       B C# D E F# G A

======================================================================================================================================================

CLEAN-ROUND STANDARD
- no missing, doubled, reversed, or reordered pair
- no pause or accent during the one-degree rollback
- correct G-string backreach, B-string offset, string changes, and assigned fingering
- both high-root notes at the turn are articulated and equal in volume
- no scrape or tempo change during a one-fret shift
- minor and major third qualities remain audible inside one connected line

VARIATIONS AFTER THE BASIC LADDER IS CLEAN
1. Accent the first note of every pair, then remove all pair accents.
2. Accent only the upper note of every pair without rushing the rollback.
3. Say m3 or M3 before every pair in one selected key.
4. Play one pair per beat, then two pairs per beat at the same metronome marking.
5. Begin selected sessions at fret 17 and descend first.
6. Choose a random root fret from 5-17, name the key, and continue either direction.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 28
NATURAL MINOR DIATONIC TRIADS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
==============================================================================================================================================

PURPOSE
Level 28 stacks one more scale tone onto the diatonic-thirds idea from Level 27. Every group now plays
a root, third, and fifth: 1-b3-5, 2-4-b6, b3-5-b7, and onward. The exercise converts natural
minor into a connected chain of broken triads while retaining the same two-octave six-string shape
and one-fret chromatic neck route.

WHAT CHANGES FROM LEVEL 27
Level 27 isolated two-note thirds and their major/minor qualities. Level 28 adds the diatonic fifth,
turning every interval pair into a complete triad. The mechanical demand becomes a three-note group
that may span one, two, or three strings; the musical demand is to hear and name i, ii diminished,
III, iv, v, VI, and VII without losing the continuous triplet pulse.

NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
One octave: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Two octaves: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8 9 b10 11 12 b13 b14 15
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole, then repeat

MAIN SEQUENCE
Ascending:  1-b3-5 | 2-4-b6 | b3-5-b7 | 4-b6-8 | 5-b7-9 | b6-8-b10 | b7-9-11 | 8-b10-12 | 9-11-b13 | b10-12-b14 | 11-b13-15
Descending: 15-b13-11 | b14-12-b10 | b13-11-9 | 12-b10-8 | 11-9-b7 | b10-8-b6 | 9-b7-5 | 8-b6-4 | b7-5-b3 | b6-4-2 | 5-b3-1
Each new triad begins one scale position farther forward. The line climbs a third and another third,
then rolls back three scale positions to begin the next chord. Do not pause or reset at the rollback.

HARMONIC FUNCTION AND QUALITY
Ascending:  i minor | ii diminished | III major | iv minor | v minor | VI major | VII major | i minor | ii diminished | III major | iv minor
Descending: iv minor | III major | ii diminished | i minor | VII major | VI major | v minor | iv minor | III major | ii diminished | i minor
Natural minor has a minor v and a major VII because degree b7 is not raised. Harmonic minor will alter
those functions later; do not import the raised seventh into this workbook.

TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4        Positions 1,2,b3
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4        Positions 4,5,b6
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3          Positions b7,8
G string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4        Positions 9,b10,11
B string:     R, R+1, R+3          Fingers 1,2,4        Positions 12,b13,b14
High e:       R                    Finger 1             Position 15
The complete map spans R-1 through R+3. Release and rebuild for the G-string backreach and again for
the B-string offset; do not hold a static five-fret stretch.

STRING-PATH MAP
Ascending:  EEA | EAA | EAD | AAD | ADG | ADG | DGG | DGB | GGB | GBB | GBe
Descending: eBG | BBG | BGG | BGD | GGD | GDA | GDA | DAA | DAE | AAE | AEE
Some triads remain on two strings, while others span three strings. Keep the middle note rhythmically
centered and every landing equal in volume through the D-G and G-B transitions.

CELL DESIGN
- 11 ascending triads / 33 notes
- repeat the high root at the turnaround as the first note of the descending line
- 11 descending triads / 33 notes
- 22 triads / 66 notes total per key
- shift the entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret only after the final 5-b3-1 triad

PICKING
Downstroke start: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U ... through all 22 triads.
Upstroke start:   U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ... through all 22 triads.
Every three-note triad flips the starting stroke of the next triad. The complete 66-note cell is even,
so every new key begins on the same pick orientation. Do not reset at group boundaries, string changes,
the middle octave, the repeated high root, or a new key.

RHYTHM
Learning pulse: one triad per beat as eighth-note triplets.
Performance pulse: two triads per beat as sixteenth-note triplets (sextuplets).
Accent the root of each triad while learning, then remove the accents and equalize every note.

PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. A natural minor, first octave only: i through iv, then reverse.
2. A natural minor, all 11 ascending triads.
3. A natural minor, all 11 descending triads.
4. Link the 66-note cell; articulate both high-root notes without resetting.
5. Use two or three neighboring keys with a one-beat pause only after each complete cell.
6. Remove the pause and complete the entire route with both pick starts.

CHROMATIC ROUTE
Up:   A -> Bb -> B -> C -> C# -> D -> Eb -> E -> F -> F# -> G -> G# -> A
Down: G# -> G -> F# -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> C# -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-natural-minor rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.

ROUTE REFERENCE
Rung  Key                          Low-E root    Frame     Diatonic triads (degrees 1-b7)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
01    A natural minor               fret 5        4-8       Am Bdim C Dm Em F G
02    Bb natural minor              fret 6        5-9       Bbm Cdim Db Ebm Fm Gb Ab
03    B natural minor               fret 7        6-10      Bm C#dim D Em F#m G A
04    C natural minor               fret 8        7-11      Cm Ddim Eb Fm Gm Ab Bb
05    C# natural minor              fret 9        8-12      C#m D#dim E F#m G#m A B
06    D natural minor               fret 10       9-13      Dm Edim F Gm Am Bb C
07    Eb natural minor              fret 11       10-14     Ebm Fdim Gb Abm Bbm Cb Db
08    E natural minor               fret 12       11-15     Em F#dim G Am Bm C D

11    G natural minor               fret 15       14-18     Gm Adim Bb Cm Dm Eb F
12    G# natural minor              fret 16       15-19     G#m A#dim B C#m D#m E F#
13    A natural minor - octave      fret 17       16-20     Am Bdim C Dm Em F G

==============================================================================================================================================
COMPLETE TABLATURE
==============================================================================================================================================

==============================================================================================================================================

CLEAN-ROUND STANDARD
- No missing, doubled, reversed, or reordered triad.
- Every chord quality matches natural minor, especially minor v and major VII.
- Correct G-string backreach, B-string offset, and assigned fingering.
- Both articulated high-root notes are equal in volume and use opposite pick strokes.
- No scrape, pause, or tempo change during any one-fret shift.
- The harmonic function remains audible as one connected line.

AFTER THE BASIC LADDER IS CLEAN
1. Accent the root of every triad, then remove all root accents.
2. Accent only the third, then only the fifth, without changing the pulse.
3. Say the Roman numeral and chord quality before every group in one selected key.
4. Play one triad per beat, then two triads per beat at the same metronome marking.
5. Begin selected sessions at fret 17 and descend first.
6. Choose a random root fret 5-17, name the key and all seven triads, then continue either direction.
These are Level 28 variations, not separate full levels.

NEXT: LEVEL 29 - NATURAL MINOR SYNTHESIS CIRCUIT
Combine the straight scale, three-note rolling sequence, four-note rolling sequence, diatonic thirds,
and diatonic triads into one uninterrupted natural-minor capstone circuit.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 29
NATURAL MINOR SYNTHESIS CIRCUIT - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
================================================================================================================================================================

PURPOSE
Level 29 combines the established two-octave natural-minor movements from Levels 22, 24, 26, 27, and 28 into
one uninterrupted circuit. Complete all five modules in the same key before shifting the entire hand-and-thumb
frame one fret. Re-articulate the low root at every module boundary while preserving the alternate-picking cycle.

FIVE-MODULE CELL
A. Linear scale:          30 notes - low root to high root, repeat high root, return to low root
B. Three-note roll:       78 notes - 13 ascending triplets and 13 descending triplets
C. Four-note roll:        96 notes - 12 ascending groups and 12 descending groups
D. Diatonic thirds:       52 notes - 13 ascending pairs and 13 descending pairs
E. Diatonic triads:       66 notes - 11 ascending triads and 11 descending triads
TOTAL:                   322 notes per key

MODULE ORDER
Linear -> Three-note roll -> Four-note roll -> Diatonic thirds -> Diatonic triads -> shift one fret

NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
One octave: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Two octaves: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8 9 b10 11 12 b13 b14 15
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole, then repeat

PICKING
All five module counts are even. With a downstroke start, every module and every new key begins on a downstroke;
with an upstroke start, each begins on an upstroke. Do not reset at group boundaries, string changes, octave turns,

Native-pulse mode:

2. Link adjacent module pairs: A-B, B-C, C-D, and D-E.

6. Complete longer route sections with both a downstroke and an upstroke start.

CLEAN-CIRCUIT STANDARD
- All five degree patterns remain in the correct order.
- The quarter-note pulse survives every subdivision change.
- Both low-root attacks at every module boundary are clear and even.
- No pick-cycle restart occurs at groups, strings, turnarounds, modules, or keys.
- The G-string backreach, B-string offset, and one-fret shifts remain silent and controlled.
- Minor/major thirds and i, ii-diminished, III, iv, v, VI, and VII triads remain audible.
- No raised seventh enters the natural-minor circuit.
- No accumulating shoulder, thumb, wrist, or forearm tension.

GRADUATION LADDER
1. One A-natural-minor circuit, module pauses allowed.
2. One A-natural-minor circuit, no pauses, both pick starts.
3. Three neighboring keys without a pulse break.
4. One six-key half-route with both pick starts.
5. Full 25-cell route on a separate endurance day.

PRACTICE VARIATIONS
- One note per click; then native pulse: eighths -> triplets -> sixteenths -> eighths -> triplets.
- Accent the first note of each group; then accent only module boundaries; finally remove every accent.
- Say each key before module 1 begins and name b3, b6, and b7 during the linear module.
- Call major or minor for every third pair.
- Call i, ii-dim, III, iv, v, VI, or VII for every triad.
- Start from a randomly selected rung and reverse direction.
- Complete separate D-start and U-start days with strict alternate picking throughout.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS AND RECOVERY
LOST SUBDIVISION: Return to one note per click, then relink only the failing module boundary.
WRONG DEGREE ORDER: Speak the numeric sequence before playing; isolate one ascending or descending half.
RAISED-SEVENTH LEAK: Stop and name b7 aloud; compare natural-minor v and VII before resuming.
NOISY BACKREACH OR SHIFT: Release pressure earlier, move the thumb with the hand, and reduce 4-6 BPM.
PICK RESET: Mute the strings and air-pick the complete note count through the boundary.
TENSION BUILDUP: Stop the circuit, shake out, lower the tempo, and use a shorter key block.

ADVANCEMENT RULES
- After one error: finish the current module, stop, and repair the exact transition.
- After two errors: reduce 4-6 BPM or shorten the route to three keys.
- After any pain or persistent tension: stop for the day; do not force the full circuit.
- Advance 2 BPM only after three clean circuits at the current route length.
- Increase route length before speed when the one-fret relocation is the weak link.
- Increase speed before route length when memory is secure but coordination is slow.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 30
MAJOR PENTATONIC ONE-OCTAVE ONE-FRET NECK LADDER: A TO A

PURPOSE
Learn one compact one-octave major-pentatonic shape, move the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every major-pentatonic key. Begin with A major pentatonic at low-E fret 5, climb to A major
pentatonic at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.

MAJOR SCALE VS MAJOR PENTATONIC
A major:             A B C# D E F# G# A
A major pentatonic:  A B C#   E F#    A
Degrees 4 and 7 are omitted. This removes the two half-step tensions 3-4 and 7-8 from the full major scale.

MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees:   1 2 3 5 6 8
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third

COMPACT ONE-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
A string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
D string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
The four-fret hand frame runs from R-1 through R+2.
Ascending notes per string: 2-2-2. Descending notes per string: 2-2-2.

CELL AND PICKING RULE
Play degrees 1-2-3-5-6-8, then 8-6-5-3-2-1. The octave root is repeated at the turn.
This creates 12 notes, so the next key begins with the same alternate-picking orientation.
D-start: D U D U D U | D U D U D U
U-start: U D U D U D | U D U D U D
Do not restart the pick cycle at the scale turn, a string crossing, or the one-fret shift.

IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed shape by one fret transposes it. A major pentatonic is the starting rung, not the key of every rung.
Holding A major pentatonic constant while connecting its five neck positions is a later branch of this section.

NECK ROUTE
UP:   A(5) > Bb(6) > B(7) > C(8) > Db(9) > D(10) > Eb(11) > E(12) > F(13) > Gb(14) > G(15) > Ab(16) > A(17)
DOWN: A(17) > Ab(16) > G(15) > Gb(14) > F(13) > E(12) > Eb(11) > D(10) > Db(9) > C(8) > B(7) > Bb(6) > A(5)

PRACTICE RULE
First compare A major and A major pentatonic and identify the omitted 4th and 7th. Then use 3-4 neighboring
major-pentatonic rungs. Play even eighth notes and pause one beat after each 12-note cell. During the pause,
release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts. Then remove the pause,
connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return to fret 5.
Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, dragged shift noise, or rising tension.
Advance after the complete route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

================================================================================================================

CLEAN-ROUND STANDARD
No open strings, no dragged shift noise, no missing scale tone, no hesitation at the balanced 2-2-2 crossings,
and no tempo change at the one-fret relocations.

AFTER THE BASIC LADDER IS CLEAN
Full-scale contrast: play one A-major cell, then one A-major-pentatonic cell; hear and locate the omitted 4 and 7.
Chord-tone focus: accent degrees 1, 3, and 5; then hear degrees 2 and 6 as color tones.
Rhythm: eighth notes, straight sixteenths, then six-note ascent and descent bursts.
Direction: begin some sessions at fret 17 and descend first.
Random entry: choose any root fret from 5-17, name the major key, play its cell, then continue either way.

NEXT LEVEL
Level 31 extends the same major-pentatonic formula across two octaves and all six strings.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 31
MAJOR PENTATONIC TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A

PURPOSE
Extend the exact Level 30 major-pentatonic frame across all six strings and two full octaves. Play the complete
22-note up/down cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret, and repeat through
every major-pentatonic key. Begin with A major pentatonic at low-E fret 5, climb to A major pentatonic at fret 17,
then reverse and return one fret at a time.

IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed shape by one fret transposes it. A major pentatonic is the starting rung, not the key of every rung.
Holding A major pentatonic constant while connecting its five positions is a later branch of Section IV.

MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees per octave: 1 2 3 5 6
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
The omitted degrees 4 and 7 remain absent in both octaves.

COMPACT TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
A string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
D string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
G string:     R-1, R+1             Fingers 1,3
B string:     R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
High e string:R                    Finger 2
The four-fret hand frame runs from R-1 through R+2.

STRING-DISTRIBUTION RULE
Ascending note counts by string: 2 - 2 - 2 - 2 - 2 - 1.
Descending note counts by string: 1 - 2 - 2 - 2 - 2 - 2.
The G-to-B tuning offset changes the visible geometry. Rebuild the assigned fingering rather than copying the
G-string shape directly onto the B and high-e strings.

CELL AND PICKING RULE
Ascend from the low root through the middle root to the high root, repeat the high root at the turnaround,
then descend to the low root. The complete cell contains 22 notes, so the next key begins with the same
alternate-picking orientation.
D-start: strict D-U alternate picking through every crossing, root, turnaround, and one-fret relocation.
U-start: strict U-D alternate picking through every crossing, root, turnaround, and one-fret relocation.
Do not restart the pick cycle on a new string, at the middle root, at the high-root turn, or after shifting.

NECK ROUTE
UP:   A(5) > Bb(6) > B(7) > C(8) > Db(9) > D(10) > Eb(11) > E(12) > F(13) > Gb(14) > G(15) > Ab(16) > A(17)
DOWN: A(17) > Ab(16) > G(15) > Gb(14) > F(13) > E(12) > Eb(11) > D(10) > Db(9) > C(8) > B(7) > Bb(6) > A(5)

PRACTICE RULE
Begin 10-15 BPM below your clean Level 30 tempo. First master the A-major-pentatonic cell alone. Then use 2-3
neighboring rungs, play even eighth notes, and pause one beat after each 22-note cell while moving the complete
frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts. Remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return
to fret 5. Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, crossing noise, dragged shifts,
or rising tension. Advance after the full route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

==========================================================================================================================

CLEAN-ROUND STANDARD
No open strings, missing pentatonic tone, unplanned doubled note, dragged shift, crossing hesitation, or volume
drop at the middle or high root. The one-fret relocations must not change the tempo.

AFTER THE LADDER IS CLEAN
Root accents: accent only the low, middle, and high roots.
Chord-tone focus: accent degrees 1, 3, and 5; hear degrees 2 and 6 as color tones.
String-entry audit: accent the first note on every new string, then remove all landing accents.
Direction: begin selected sessions at fret 17 and descend first.
Random entry: choose any root fret from 5-17, name the key, and continue either way.

NEXT LEVEL
Level 32 begins major-pentatonic sequence studies, using short three-note cells and full five-note groups.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 32
MAJOR PENTATONIC THREE-NOTE ROLL AND FIVE-NOTE CYCLE - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A

PURPOSE
Keep the Level 31 two-octave major-pentatonic frame and reorganize its eleven ordered scale positions
into two overlapping odd-count sequence modules. Practice each module separately, then link both modules
before moving the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret. Begin with A major pentatonic at low-E
fret 5, climb to the octave A at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.

MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees per octave: 1 2 3 5 6 8
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
The complete two-octave position line is: 1 2 3 5 6 8 9 10 12 13 15.

TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
A string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
D string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
G string:     R-1, R+1             Fingers 1,3
B string:     R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
High e string: R                   Finger 2
The four-fret frame runs from R-1 through R+2. Do not change the Level 31 fingering.

MODULE A - THREE-NOTE ROLL
UP:   1-2-3 | 2-3-5 | 3-5-6 | 5-6-8 | 6-8-9 | 8-9-10 | 9-10-12 | 10-12-13 | 12-13-15
DOWN: 15-13-12 | 13-12-10 | 12-10-9 | 10-9-8 | 9-8-6 | 8-6-5 | 6-5-3 | 5-3-2 | 3-2-1
Each new triplet begins one pentatonic position farther along. The module contains 18 triplets and 54 notes.
Native grouped pulse: one eighth-note triplet per beat.
String paths up:   EEA | EAA | AAD | ADD | DDG | DGG | GGB | GBB | BBe
String paths down: eBB | BBG | BGG | GGD | GDD | DDA | DAA | AAE | AEE

MODULE B - FIVE-NOTE CYCLE
UP:   1-2-3-5-6 | 2-3-5-6-8 | 3-5-6-8-9 | 5-6-8-9-10 | 6-8-9-10-12 | 8-9-10-12-13 | 9-10-12-13-15
DOWN: 15-13-12-10-9 | 13-12-10-9-8 | 12-10-9-8-6 | 10-9-8-6-5 | 9-8-6-5-3 | 8-6-5-3-2 | 6-5-3-2-1
Each group contains five consecutive pentatonic positions and restarts one position farther along.
The module contains 14 quintuplets and 70 notes. Native grouped pulse: one quintuplet per beat.
String paths up:   EEAAD | EAADD | AADDG | ADDGG | DDGGB | DGGBB | GGBBe
String paths down: eBBGG | BBGGD | BGGDD | GGDDA | GDDAA | DDAAE | DAAEE

PICKING AND CELL RULE
Every three-note or five-note group is odd, so the starting stroke reverses at the next group.
Module A D-start: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ...
Module B D-start: D-U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U-D ...
Use the mirrored patterns for an upstroke start. Module A has 54 notes and Module B has 70 notes; both
totals are even. Therefore Module B and every new key begin with the original pick orientation.
Do not reset the pick at a group, string crossing, middle root, high-root turn, module boundary, or shift.

RHYTHM MODES
Grouped mode: one triplet or one quintuplet per beat. Learn this version first.
Displacement mode: play continuous sixteenth notes and let the three- or five-note group accent migrate
across 4/4. Treat displacement as a variation only after the grouped pulse is secure.

NECK ROUTE
UP:   A(5) > Bb(6) > B(7) > C(8) > Db(9) > D(10) > Eb(11) > E(12) > F(13) > Gb(14) > G(15) > Ab(16) > A(17)
DOWN: A(17) > Ab(16) > G(15) > Gb(14) > F(13) > E(12) > Eb(11) > D(10) > Db(9) > C(8) > B(7) > Bb(6) > A(5)

COUNTS
Module A: 54 notes / 18 beats per key; 25-cell round trip = 1,350 notes.
Module B: 70 notes / 14 beats per key; 25-cell round trip = 1,750 notes.
Linked A+B: 124 notes / 32 beats per key; 25-cell round trip = 3,100 notes / 800 beats.

====================================================================================================================================
RUNG 01 OF 13 - A MAJOR PENTATONIC - ROOT ON LOW E FRET 5 - FRAME 4-7
Two-octave tones: A B C# E F# A B C# E F# A

====================================================================================================================================
SEVEN-PHASE PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Play the Level 31 A-major-pentatonic frame once up and down.
2. Practice the first-octave Module A groups before using all six strings.
3. Play the complete 54-note Module A with one note per click, then one triplet per beat.
4. Practice the first two Module B windows in the lower octave.
5. Play the complete 70-note Module B with one note per click, then one quintuplet per beat.
6. In A only, play Module A immediately followed by Module B without a pause or pick reset.
7. Use three-key blocks; then connect the full fret-5 to fret-17 to fret-5 route.

AUDIT AND REPAIR
Lost group: speak the degree window aloud and loop only the two groups surrounding the error.
Rushed subdivision: return to one note per click and rebuild equal notes without a first-note accent.
Crossing accent: accent the landing deliberately, then remove it while preserving the movement.
Pick reset: mute the strings and air-pick the complete module through the failing boundary.
Shift scrape: release pressure before moving, move the thumb with the frame, and reduce 4-6 BPM.

NEXT LEVEL
Level 33 leaves consecutive pentatonic windows and begins interval pairs and melodic skips.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 33
MAJOR PENTATONIC INTERVAL PAIRS AND MELODIC SKIPS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A

PURPOSE
Keep the Level 31 two-octave major-pentatonic frame and reorganize its eleven ordered scale positions into
two interval-focused modules. Module A skips one pentatonic tone to create adjacent-string interval pairs.
Module B makes a wider leap, then resolves to the skipped upper tone. Practice each module separately, link
both modules, then move the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret. Begin with A major pentatonic
at low-E fret 5, climb to the octave A at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.

MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees per octave: 1 2 3 5 6
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
Two-octave ordered positions: 1 2 3 5 6 8 9 10 12 13 15.

TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string:  R, R+2               Fingers 2,4                  Positions 1,2
A string:      R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4                  Positions 3,5
D string:      R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4                  Positions 6,8
G string:      R-1, R+1             Fingers 1,3                  Positions 9,10
B string:      R, R+2               Fingers 2,4                  Positions 12,13
High e string: R                    Finger 2                     Position 15
The four-fret frame runs from R-1 through R+2. Do not change the Level 31 fingering.

MODULE A - SKIP-ONE INTERVAL PAIRS
UP:   1-3 | 2-5 | 3-6 | 5-8 | 6-9 | 8-10 | 9-12 | 10-13 | 12-15
INT:  M3  | P4  | P4  | P4  | P4  | M3   | P4   | P4    | P4
DOWN: 15-12 | 13-10 | 12-9 | 10-8 | 9-6 | 8-5 | 6-3 | 5-2 | 3-1
Each pair skips one pentatonic position and lands on the next physical string. The module contains 18 pairs
and 36 notes. Native pulse: one two-note pair per beat as eighth notes.
String paths up:   EA | EA | AD | AD | DG | DG | GB | GB | Be
String paths down: eB | BG | BG | GD | GD | DA | DA | AE | AE

MODULE B - WIDE-LEAP RESOLVE
UP:   1-5-3 | 2-6-5 | 3-8-6 | 5-9-8 | 6-10-9 | 8-12-10 | 9-13-12 | 10-15-13
DOWN: 15-10-12 | 13-9-10 | 12-8-9 | 10-6-8 | 9-5-6 | 8-3-5 | 6-2-3 | 5-1-2
The first two notes leap across three ordered pentatonic positions; the third note resolves to the skipped
upper position. First-leap qualities are P5 or m6. Resolution qualities are M2 or m3. The module contains
16 triplets and 48 notes. Native pulse: one eighth-note triplet per beat.
String paths up:   EAA | EDA | ADD | AGD | DGG | DBG | GBB | GeB
String paths down: eGB | BGG | BDG | GDD | GAD | DAA | DEA | AEE

PICKING AND CELL RULE
Module A uses even two-note groups, so every pair begins with the original pick orientation.
Module B uses odd three-note groups, so the group-starting stroke alternates at every boundary.
Module A contains 36 notes and Module B contains 48 notes; both totals are even. Therefore Module B and
every new key begin with the original starting stroke. Do not reset at a pair, triplet, string crossing,
skipped string, middle root, high-root turn, module boundary, or one-fret shift.
A D-start: D-U | D-U | D-U ...
B D-start: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ...
Use the mirrored patterns for an upstroke start.

RHYTHM MODES
Grouped mode: Module A = one eighth-note pair per beat; Module B = one eighth-note triplet per beat.
Displacement mode: after the grouped pulse is secure, play continuous sixteenth notes and let the accents
move through 4/4 without changing the degree order.

NECK ROUTE
UP:   A(5) > Bb(6) > B(7) > C(8) > Db(9) > D(10) > Eb(11) > E(12) > F(13) > Gb(14) > G(15) > Ab(16) > A(17)
DOWN: A(17) > Ab(16) > G(15) > Gb(14) > F(13) > E(12) > Eb(11) > D(10) > Db(9) > C(8) > B(7) > Bb(6) > A(5)

COUNTS
Module A: 36 notes / 18 beats per key; 25-cell round trip = 900 notes.
Module B: 48 notes / 16 beats per key; 25-cell round trip = 1,200 notes.
Linked A+B: 84 notes / 34 beats per key; 25-cell round trip = 2,100 notes / 850 beats.

====================================================================================================================================
RUNG 01 OF 13 - A MAJOR PENTATONIC - ROOT ON LOW E FRET 5 - FRAME 4-7
Two-octave tones: A B C# E F# A B C# E F# A

====================================================================================================================================
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Review the Level 31 A-major-pentatonic cell once up and down.
2. Practice Module A in A. Say M3 or P4 before each pair.
3. Repeat Module A with a downstroke start and an upstroke start.
4. Practice the first four Module B groups in the lower octave.
5. Complete Module B and say P5 or m6 on the first leap of each group.
6. Link Module A and Module B in one key without a pause.
7. Use three-key blocks, then climb to fret 17, reverse, and return to fret 5.

HEARING TARGETS
Module A: positions 1-3 and 8-10 form M3; the remaining skip-one pairs form P4.
Module B: most first leaps form P5; positions 3-8 and 10-15 form m6.
The third note resolves to the skipped pentatonic position by M2 or m3.

AUDIT AND REPAIR
PAIR SOUNDS STEPWISE: Say the two degrees first and confirm that one pentatonic tone is skipped.
WRONG INTERVAL NAME: Stop on the two notes, sing the upper note, then call M3/P4 or P5/m6.
SKIPPED-STRING NOISE: Reduce pick depth, mute the unused string, and isolate the first two notes.
RESOLUTION RUSHED: Accent note 3 deliberately, then repeat all notes at equal volume.
PICK RESET: Mute the strings and air-pick one complete module through every boundary.
SHIFT SCRAPE: Release pressure before moving the hand and thumb; reduce 4-6 BPM.

PRACTICE LOG
Date ______  BPM A ____  BPM B ____  Start stroke ____  Clean route? ____
Weak pair / leap ______________________________  Next target ______________________________

NEXT: Level 34 holds A major pentatonic constant and connects its five common neck positions.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 34
A MAJOR PENTATONIC FIVE-POSITION CONNECTION - FIXED-KEY NECK MAP

PURPOSE
Stop transposing one shape. Keep the key fixed as A major pentatonic and move through five common
positions from the low-E root frame at frets 4-7 through the octave frame at frets 14-17. Learn each
vertical position, connect adjacent positions around one shared anchor note on every string, then link
all five frames in a forward and reverse zigzag.

IMPORTANT POSITION-LABEL NOTE
Pentatonic box numbers vary among methods. This workbook numbers positions in ascending-neck order,
beginning with the A-root frame around low-E fret 5. Use the fret spans, degree maps, and root locations
as the authoritative identity of each position.

A MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third

POSITION SUMMARY
P1 ROOT FRAME             frets 4-7    starts degree 1  roots E5, D7, e5
    Ascending degrees: 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2
P2 SECOND-DEGREE FRAME    frets 6-10   starts degree 2  roots D7, B10
    Ascending degrees: 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3
P3 THIRD-DEGREE FRAME     frets 9-12   starts degree 3  roots A12, B10
    Ascending degrees: 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5
P4 FIFTH-DEGREE FRAME     frets 11-14  starts degree 5  roots A12, G14
    Ascending degrees: 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6
P5 SIXTH-DEGREE FRAME     frets 14-17  starts degree 6  roots E17, G14, e17
    Ascending degrees: 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1

PICKING AND COUNTS
Each vertical position cell contains 24 notes: 12 ascending and 12 descending with the high endpoint repeated.
Each shared-anchor seam cell contains 30 notes: six five-note string groups. Every five-note group flips the
starting stroke on the next string, but the complete 30-note cell is even.
The forward zigzag contains 60 notes; the reverse zigzag contains 60 notes. Repeat high-e fret 17 at the
turn when linking them, producing an even 120-note circuit.
Five position cells = 120 notes. Four seam cells = 120 notes. Linked zigzag = 120 notes.
Complete Level 34 workout = 360 notes.

STRICT ALTERNATE PICKING
Complete separate D-start and U-start passes. Do not restart at a string crossing, shared anchor, position
boundary, root, outer-string turn, or the forward/reverse turnaround.

========================================================================================================================
FIVE VERTICAL POSITION CELLS
========================================================================================================================

========================================================================================================================
SHARED-ANCHOR SEAM CELLS
========================================================================================================================
For each string, play lower outer note -> shared anchor -> upper outer note -> shared anchor -> lower outer note.
Stay in the lower-position fingering through note 2. Shift after the anchor sounds, play note 3 in the upper
frame, return to the anchor as note 4, then shift back before note 5. Do not re-articulate the anchor merely
to disguise the hand movement.

========================================================================================================================
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Map P1-P5 and say each starting degree.
2. Play every 24-note vertical cell with both pick starts.
3. Learn all four 30-note shared-anchor seam cells.
4. Play the 60-note forward zigzag without a seam pause.
5. Play the 60-note reverse zigzag without a seam pause.
6. Link forward and reverse as one 120-note circuit.
7. Accent every A root, then remove the accents while continuing to hear A as tonic.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
LOST KEY CENTER: Stop on the nearest A root, sing A, and restart the local frame.
WRONG BOX: Name the position span and its first low-E degree before playing.
EARLY SHIFT: Remain in the lower frame through the shared anchor; move only after it sounds.
NOISY SEAM: Release pressure, move the thumb with the hand, and reduce the tempo by 4-6 BPM.
PICK RESET: Mute the strings and air-pick the exact 12-, 30-, or 60-note count.
TENSION: Stop, shake out, and practice one seam instead of forcing the full route.

ADVANCEMENT RULES
Add 2 BPM after three clean circuits at the current route length.
After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or shorten the route to one adjacent-position seam.
Increase route length before speed when the shift is weak. Increase speed before route length when the map is secure.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 35
A MAJOR PENTATONIC HORIZONTAL STRING LANES - CONTROLLED SHIFTS, SLIDES, AND DESTINATION LANDINGS

PURPOSE
Keep the key fixed as A major pentatonic and turn the five vertical positions from Level 34 into six
horizontal one-string melodies. First relocate silently between three two-note stations, then isolate one
timed slide at each of the four position seams, then land directly on named destinations over increasing
distances. Finish by linking all six strings in a forward and reverse horizontal snake.

IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
This level does not transpose the shape. Every note belongs to A major pentatonic: A B C# E F#.
The suggested route fingerings are designed for continuous one-string movement and therefore do not always
match the vertical-box fingerings from Level 34. The fret, note, degree, and timing are authoritative.

A MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
Notes:   A B C# E F#
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third

HORIZONTAL LANE SUMMARY
Low E   frets 5 7 9 12 14 17     degrees 1 2 3 5 6 1  notes A B C# E F# A    fingers 1 3 1 4 1 4 roots 5,17
A       frets 4 7 9 12 14 16     degrees 3 5 6 1 2 3  notes C# E F# A B C#   fingers 1 4 1 4 1 3 roots 12
D       frets 4 7 9 11 14 16     degrees 6 1 2 3 5 6  notes F# A B C# E F#   fingers 1 4 1 3 1 3 roots 7
G       frets 4 6 9 11 14 16     degrees 2 3 5 6 1 2  notes B C# E F# A B    fingers 1 3 1 3 1 3 roots 14
B       frets 5 7 10 12 14 17    degrees 5 6 1 2 3 5  notes E F# A B C# E    fingers 1 3 1 3 1 4 roots 10
High e  frets 5 7 9 12 14 17     degrees 1 2 3 5 6 1  notes A B C# E F# A    fingers 1 3 1 4 1 4 roots 5,17

PICKING AND COUNT RULES
Module A: six 12-note picked cells = 72 picked notes.
Module B: 24 slide phrases x 6 sounding tones = 144 sounding tones, but only 96 pick attacks.
Module C: six 16-note destination ladders = 96 picked notes.
Module D: forward 36 + reverse 36 = 72 picked notes.
Complete Level 35 workout = 384 sounding tones / 336 pick attacks.

STRICT ALTERNATE PICKING
Complete separate D-start and U-start passes. Do not restart at a string change, station shift, seam slide,
repeated destination, A root, or forward/reverse turnaround. A slide destination is sounded without a new
pick attack and must arrive exactly on the subdivision.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE A - SIX SILENT-SHIFT HORIZONTAL LANES
========================================================================================================================
Group each lane into three two-note stations. Use finger 1-3 for a whole step and 1-4 for a minor third.
Shift after the first station and after the second station. Release pressure before moving. No slide is allowed.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE B - TIMED POSITION-SEAM SLIDES
========================================================================================================================
For every string: pick the lower note; pick the shared anchor and slide to the upper destination; re-pick the
destination and slide back to the anchor; pick the lower note. Each phrase contains 6 sounding tones but
only 4 pick attacks. Use finger 3 for a two-fret slide and finger 4 for a three-fret slide.

SEAM P1 -> P2
String tab                  Degree path         Note path               Slide finger   Destination

Timing rule: the destination must arrive on the subdivision; do not add an extra pick at the slide arrival.

SEAM P2 -> P3
String tab                  Degree path         Note path               Slide finger   Destination

Timing rule: the destination must arrive on the subdivision; do not add an extra pick at the slide arrival.

SEAM P3 -> P4
String tab                  Degree path         Note path               Slide finger   Destination

Timing rule: the destination must arrive on the subdivision; do not add an extra pick at the slide arrival.

SEAM P4 -> P5
String tab                  Degree path         Note path               Slide finger   Destination

Timing rule: the destination must arrive on the subdivision; do not add an extra pick at the slide arrival.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE C - DESTINATION-NOTE LANDINGS
========================================================================================================================
Launch from the lower endpoint of each string. Land on the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth lane notes in turn.
Each four-note cell is launch -> target -> repeated target -> launch. First pass: use finger 1 on every note.
No slide is allowed. After the printed pass, begin at the upper endpoint and mirror the target order downward.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE D - FORWARD AND REVERSE SIX-STRING HORIZONTAL SNAKE
========================================================================================================================
Every segment contains six notes. Because six is even, each new string begins with the original pick-start
orientation. Do not reset at a string change.

========================================================================================================================
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Map all six lanes and say notes plus degrees.
2. Play one Module A lane at one note per click.
3. Complete all six silent-shift cells with both pick starts.
4. Add one seam-slide page; count 6 tones but only 4 attacks per string.
5. Complete Module C with finger 1 and no audible relocation.
6. Play the 36-note forward snake without a pause.
7. Play the 36-note reverse snake without a pause.
8. Link the 72-note circuit and accent every A root, then remove the accents.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
NOISY SHIFT: release earlier, move the thumb with the hand, and reduce 4-6 BPM.
LATE SLIDE: shorten the motion and practice the anchor-to-target pair alone.
FRET FISHING: name and look at the destination before leaving the launch note.
PICK RESET: mute the strings and air-pick the exact 12-, 36-, or 72-note count.
TENSION: stop the full route and return to one string.

ADVANCEMENT RULES
Add 2 BPM after three clean runs at the current route length. After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or shorten
the route to one lane or seam. Increase route length before speed when the map is weak. Increase speed
before route length only when every destination is already secure.

PRACTICE LOG

NEXT LEVEL

controlled slides, bends, releases, and vibrato.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 36
A MAJOR PENTATONIC EXPRESSIVE ARTICULATION - LEGATO, SLIDES, BENDS, RELEASES, AND VIBRATO
FIXED KEY A - FIVE POSITIONS - FRETS 4-17

PURPOSE
Turn the fixed-key A-major-pentatonic map from Levels 34-35 into controlled expressive motion. The pitch map
does not change. What changes is how each pitch begins, connects, bends, releases, and sustains. Train hammer-ons
and pull-offs in all five positions, combine legato with the four shared-anchor seams, calibrate whole-step bends
against named target frets, add pre-bend releases and pitch-centered vibrato, then finish with five short cadences.

IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Expression does not excuse inaccurate rhythm or pitch. A hammer-on, pull-off, slide arrival, bend target, release,
or vibrato pulse is a timed musical event. Picked and unpicked notes must remain equal in volume and duration.
All core bends in this level are whole-step bends to a note two frets higher. The minor-third gaps 3->5 and 6->1
would require a one-and-a-half-step bend and are deliberately excluded from the core bend module.

A MAJOR PENTATONIC
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6

ARTICULATION NOTATION
h = hammer-on; p = pull-off; / = ascending slide; \ = descending slide; b(T) = bend to target fret T;
r = release; pb(T) = pre-bend silently to target pitch before the attack; ~ = vibrato.

COUNTS
Module A: 5 position cells x 24 sounding tones = 120 tones; 12 attacks per cell = 60 attacks.
Module B: 4 seams x 6 strings x 5 tones = 120 tones; one attack per phrase = 24 attacks.
Module C: 9 whole-step bend sites x 4 attacks = 36 attacks.
Module D: 6 pre-bend cells x 3 attacks = 18 attacks; 8 A-root vibrato holds = 8 attacks.
Module E: 5 cadence phrases = 19 attacks; articulation creates the remaining pitch motion.
Complete core workout: 165 pick attacks, plus 240 explicitly counted legato/slide tones, 15 bend or pre-bend
cells, 8 root-vibrato holds, and 5 cadence phrases.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE A - FIVE-POSITION LEGATO CELLS
========================================================================================================================
Pick the first tone of each two-note group. Hammer the ascending partner and pull off the descending partner.
Each position contains 12 groups, 24 sounding tones, and 12 pick attacks. Alternate the group attacks continuously.
D-start groups: D U D U D U | D U D U D U. U-start groups: U D U D U D | U D U D U D.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE B - ONE-PICK FIVE-TONE SEAM CHAINS
========================================================================================================================
Phrase rule: lower note h shared anchor / upper note \ shared anchor p lower note. Pick only the first tone.
Do not hold a rigid wide stretch at the outer destination. Release the lower finger during the outward slide and
replant it during the return so the final pull-off is prepared. First use one tone per click; later use quintuplets.

SEAM P1 <-> P2

One phrase = 5 sounding tones / 1 pick attack. The slide arrival and final pull-off remain on the subdivision.

SEAM P2 <-> P3

One phrase = 5 sounding tones / 1 pick attack. The slide arrival and final pull-off remain on the subdivision.

SEAM P3 <-> P4

One phrase = 5 sounding tones / 1 pick attack. The slide arrival and final pull-off remain on the subdivision.

SEAM P4 <-> P5

One phrase = 5 sounding tones / 1 pick attack. The slide arrival and final pull-off remain on the subdivision.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE C - WHOLE-STEP BEND INTONATION
========================================================================================================================
Core cell: play the target fret; play the source and bend to the target; play the source and bend-release;
finish by re-playing the target with narrow vibrato. Four attacks per site. Bend toward the center of the neck.
Use the ring finger supported by the index and middle fingers where practical. Mute adjacent strings.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE D - PRE-BEND RELEASES AND PITCH-CENTERED VIBRATO
========================================================================================================================
Pre-bend rule: reach the target pitch silently before attacking. The listener should hear the target first, then the
controlled release. The final bend reaches the same target and adds narrow vibrato only after the pitch is stable.

Vibrato passes: 4 pulses per whole note; 6 pulses per whole note; then free vibrato while returning to the
original pitch between pulses. On a bent note, reach the target first and vibrate around that target.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE E - FIVE POSITION EXPRESSIVE CADENCES
========================================================================================================================

Linking rule: practice each cadence alone, then play P1-P5 with one bar of rest between phrases. Finally remove
the rests. Continue alternate picking through the actual attacks; do not add an attack to a hammer, pull, slide,
bend arrival, release, or held vibrato note.

========================================================================================================================
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Map the notation and say the A-major-pentatonic notes and degrees before playing.
2. Complete one Position 1 legato cell at one sounding tone per click.
3. Play all five Module A cells with both D-start and U-start attack cycles.
4. Add one seam page; keep all five tones equal from a single attack.
5. Calibrate one bend site by alternating the fretted target and bent target.
6. Complete all nine bend cells without overshooting, sagging, or adjacent-string noise.
7. Add pre-bend releases, then the eight A-root vibrato holds.
8. Play the five cadences separately, then link them without extra attacks.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
WEAK HAMMER: strike closer to the fret with less travel; do not squeeze harder with the thumb.
EMPTY PULL-OFF: keep the destination fretted and use a tiny lateral pluck rather than simply lifting.
LATE SLIDE: shorten the motion; the arrival fret is a counted tone, not transportation.
FLAT BEND: support the bending finger, rotate the wrist, and compare directly with the target fret.
SHARP BEND: stop pushing after the target; hold the pitch before adding vibrato.
WIDE VIBRATO: reduce the motion until every pulse returns to the pitch center.
STRING NOISE: mute above the bend with the fretting index and below it with the picking hand.
PAIN OR TENSION: stop. Do not force the whole-step bend or substitute a one-and-a-half-step bend.

ADVANCEMENT RULES
Add 2 BPM after three clean runs at the current module length. After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or isolate one
string, seam, bend, or cadence. Intonation outranks speed. Use a clean tone until the pitch and muting are stable.

PRACTICE LOG

NEXT LEVEL
Level 37 applies A major pentatonic to I-IV-V harmony, targeting chord tones over A, D, and E major instead of
treating every scale tone as equally stable.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 37
A MAJOR PENTATONIC I-IV-V CHORD-TONE TARGETING AND VOICE LEADING
FIXED KEY A - FIVE POSITIONS - A, D, AND E MAJOR HARMONY

PURPOSE
Turn the fixed-key A-major-pentatonic map into harmony-aware phrasing. Keep the same five notes and five positions,
but stop treating every note as equally stable. Hear the active I, IV, or V chord; land on a strong chord tone at
the change; use the remaining pentatonic notes as motion; then resolve before the harmony changes again.

A MAJOR PENTATONIC
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
I-IV-V chords: A major = A C# E; D major = D F# A; E major = E G# B.

CORE TARGETS AVAILABLE INSIDE A MAJOR PENTATONIC
I - A major: A root, C# third, E fifth.
IV - D major: F# third, A fifth. The D root is not in A major pentatonic.
V - E major: E root, B fifth. The G# third is not in A major pentatonic.
Module D adds D and G# temporarily as chord-completion tones; they are not new pentatonic degrees.

CHORD-ROLE MATRIX
Note | Over A | Over D | Over E
A    | R      | 5      | 11    
B    | 9      | 13     | 5     
C#   | 3      | M7     | 13    
E    | 5      | 9      | R     
F#   | 13     | 3      | 9     
A over E functions as 11/sus4 tension. C# over D functions as major-7 tension. Use either as motion, not an
unresolved downbeat landing, until the ear clearly hears the intended color.

COUNTS
Module A chord-target cells: 168 notes.
Module B voice-leading routes: 60 held tones.
Module C five position phrases: 160 eighth notes.
Module D chord-completion cadences: 60 quarter notes.
Module E model 12-bar chorus: 48 quarter notes.
Complete written workout: 496 sounding tones before optional articulation overlays.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE A - FIVE-POSITION CHORD-TARGET CELLS
========================================================================================================================
Play every target in the position from low to high, repeat the highest target, then return. Every cell is even.
Practice with D-start and U-start. Say the chord role of every note: root, third, or fifth.

P1 - ROOT FRAME - FRETS 4-7

========================================================================================================================
MODULE B - NEAREST-TARGET VOICE LEADING THROUGH | A | D | E | A |
========================================================================================================================
First hold one whole note per bar. Then add two eighth-note pickup notes before each new landing while keeping the
printed target on beat 1. The coordinate in parentheses is string plus fret.

P1 - ROOT FRAME - FRETS 4-7

========================================================================================================================
MODULE C - FIVE FOUR-BAR TARGET PHRASES
========================================================================================================================
Progression: | A | D | E | A |. Eight eighth notes per bar. The role row marks the first note of each bar with >.
Play straight first. On a second pass, add no more than one Level-36 articulation per bar without changing targets.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE D - CHORD-COMPLETION TONES: D OVER IV AND G# OVER V
========================================================================================================================
A major pentatonic does not contain the IV root D or the V third G#. Add them only while their chord is sounding,
then return to the five-note pool. An asterisk marks a completion tone outside A major pentatonic.
Position | D choices | G# choices
P1       | A5, G7             | E4, D6, e4
P2       | G7, E10, e10       | D6, B9
P3       | E10, D12, e10      | A11, B9
P4       | D12, B15           | A11, G13
P5       | B15, D12           | E16, e16, G13

CADENCE: | D | E | A |. Four quarter notes per bar. D* and G#* complete the chord.

PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Speak the I-IV-V chord tones and the five-note role matrix.
2. Complete one Position-1 target cell for each chord with both pick starts.
3. Play all fifteen target cells; hear the active chord before each cell.
4. Hold the three voice-leading routes as whole notes in all five positions.
5. Play one four-bar phrase and verify every beat-1 landing.
6. Add all five phrases, then one Level-36 articulation per bar.
7. Add D* and G#* through the five completion cadences.
8. Complete the 12-bar model chorus, then create a new fill while preserving its targets.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
SCALE-RUN AUTOPILOT: stop the fill; play only one whole-note target per chord.
WEAK CHORD CHANGE: sing the next target before the bar arrives; reduce the fill to two notes.
D-CHORD C# LANDING: treat C# as major-7 tension and resolve immediately to D*, B, or a printed strong target.
E-CHORD A LANDING: treat A as suspended 11 tension and resolve to G#*, B, or E.
FRET SEARCH: name the string and fret before leaving the current target.
OVERFILLED BAR: leave beat 4 empty; silence is part of the phrase.
PICK OR ARTICULATION RESET: preserve the target rhythm first; expression is secondary.

NEXT LEVEL
Level 38 combines the five positions, horizontal movement, articulation, and I-IV-V targeting into call-and-response
phrasing and controlled improvisation synthesis.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 38
A MAJOR PENTATONIC CALL-AND-RESPONSE PHRASING AND IMPROVISATION SYNTHESIS
FIXED KEY A - FIVE POSITIONS - HARMONY A, D, AND E MAJOR

PURPOSE
Combine the five fixed-key positions, horizontal movement, expressive articulation, and I-IV-V chord targets
into phrases that sound intentional rather than like scale recitation. Build a short call, leave measured space,
answer the active harmony, develop one recognizable motif, and preserve the chord change while moving across the neck.

A MAJOR PENTATONIC
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
I-IV-V chords: A major = A C# E; D major = D F# A; E major = E G# B.
Strong pentatonic targets: A/C#/E over A; F#/A over D; E/B over E.
Completion tones: D* may appear only over D major; G#* may appear only over E major.

PHRASE GRAMMAR
A call states a rhythm and contour, then leaves room. It often ends on degree 2 or 6 rather than a final tonic.
A response may echo the rhythm, reverse the contour, move to a neighboring position, or change the chord target.
Silence is counted. A rest is not lost time; it is part of the phrase. A response should arrive because the harmony
changed, not because the player ran out of scale notes.

TAB LEGEND
P = picked attack; h = hammer-on destination; p = pull-off destination; s = slide destination;
b = bend destination; r = rest; = = held tone. Continue alternate picking only through actual picked attacks.
The count row shows eighth-note slots: 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &.

CORE WRITTEN COUNTS
Module A local question/answer pairs: 55 sounding tones / 37 pick attacks.
Module B four seam phrases: 97 sounding tones / 62 pick attacks.
Module C motif transformation lab: 30 sounding tones / 23 pick attacks.
Module D space and density ladder: 60 sounding tones / 60 pick attacks.
Module E model 12-bar chorus: 70 sounding tones / 55 pick attacks.
Complete written workout: 312 sounding tones / 237 pick attacks, before the controlled free choruses.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE A - FIVE LOCAL QUESTION-AND-ANSWER PAIRS
========================================================================================================================
Each call and response uses one position and two bars of eighth-note slots. The call leaves an open color;
the response preserves enough of the rhythm to sound related and ends on an A-major chord tone. Practice the call,
count one full bar of silence, play the response, then remove the extra bar while keeping the phrase boundary audible.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE B - FOUR I-IV-V SEAM PHRASES
========================================================================================================================
Progression for every phrase: | A | D | E | A |. Bars 1 and 3 ask; bars 2 and 4 answer.
The lower and upper positions must sound like one melodic idea. Preserve the beat-1 chord target even when a slide,
bend, hammer, or pull changes the number of pick attacks.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE D - SPACE AND DENSITY LADDER
========================================================================================================================
Progression: | A | D | E | A |. The beat-1 targets and final A remain fixed while the number of tones changes.
Sparse contains 3 tones per bar, medium contains 5, and dense contains 7. Do not interpret density as difficulty:
the sparse version is passed only when every rest is deliberate and the harmony remains audible.

PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Clap and speak the call/response rhythm before touching the guitar.
2. Complete all five local pairs; exaggerate the silence between sentences.
3. Play the four seam phrases and verify every beat-1 target.
4. Perform the seed plus all six transformation options without changing tempo.
5. Play sparse, medium, and dense versions at one unchanged BPM.
6. Learn the 12-bar model chorus in four-bar blocks, then link the full route.
7. Replace only response bars while preserving the written calls.
8. Record the three-chorus capstone and score it before increasing tempo.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
CALL AND RESPONSE SOUND IDENTICAL: change one element only - target, contour, position, density, or articulation.
RESPONSE ARRIVES LATE: sing the target before the barline and shorten the call by one note.
NO SPACE: remove beat 4 from every call and one additional beat from every response.
MOTIF DISAPPEARS: keep the rhythm fixed and change only the ending target.
POSITION SHIFT SOUNDS LIKE A BREAK: isolate the final call note, seam movement, and first response target.
BEND OR SLIDE HIDES THE PULSE: remove the articulation; restore subdivision; add it back after timing is clean.
D* OR G#* LEAKS INTO THE WRONG CHORD: return to the five-note pool and rehearse the 12-bar target schedule aloud.
TENSION OR PANIC: stop the free chorus, return to one four-bar phrase, and reduce 4-6 BPM.

ADVANCEMENT RULES
Harmony, phrase identity, timing, and pitch control outrank speed. Add 2 BPM after three clean choruses at the
current constraint. After two missed targets or lost phrase boundaries, shorten to four bars or reduce 4-6 BPM.
Use clean tone until the rests, landings, slides, bends, and muting are reliable.

NEXT SECTION
Section V re-centers the same fretboard logic around minor pentatonic and blues vocabulary, beginning with the
relative-minor relationship before adding the blues note, minor-key bends, dominant-blues phrasing, and applications.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 39
F# MINOR PENTATONIC RELATIVE-MINOR RE-CENTERING - SAME FIVE NOTES, NEW TONIC

PURPOSE
Keep the complete A-major-pentatonic neck map from Levels 30-38, rename every note from the viewpoint of F# minor, and make F# sound like home through drone, accent, phrase ending, and repetition. No new fret or pitch is added.

SHARED PITCH POOL
A major pentatonic:  A B C# E F#   = 1 2 3 5 6
F# minor pentatonic: F# A B C# E   = 1 b3 4 5 b7
Pitch-role map:
  A   A major  1   |   F# minor b3
  B   A major  2   |   F# minor  4
  C#  A major  3   |   F# minor  5
  E   A major  5   |   F# minor b7
  F#  A major  6   |   F# minor  1

POSITION LABEL RULE
P1-P5 remain the established Level 34 ascending-neck labels. Do not renumber the boxes. The tonal center changes; the fret map and position identities do not.

F# ROOT ATLAS
Low E 14 | A 9 | D 4 and 16 | G 11 | B 7 | high e 14
P5 is the strongest tonic frame because it begins on low-E fret 14, F#.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE A - A-DRONE / F#-DRONE COMPARISON
========================================================================================================================
Play every eight-note phrase once over A and once over F#. Keep the notes, fingering, rhythm, articulation, and dynamics unchanged.
Shared note contour: B C# E F# A F# E C#

MODULE G - RANDOM-CENTER EAR TEST
========================================================================================================================
Cover the answers. Play every five-note card twice and identify the more convincing tonic before checking.

========================================================================================================================
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Memorize the dual-degree identity table.
2. Locate every F# root without playing a scale.
3. Complete all five drone-comparison phrases.
4. Read all five vertical boxes in both degree systems.
5. Play every F# root-to-root cell with D-start and U-start.
6. Relocate the accents from A to F# without changing rhythm.
7. Perform every cadence pair and the eight-bar tonic pivot.
8. Complete the no-drone ear test and record one free F#-minor-centered phrase.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
A STILL SOUNDS LIKE HOME: begin in P5, hold an F# drone, and play only root-to-root cells.
WRONG DEGREE NAME: point to the note and say both jobs before resuming the pick.
ACCENT CHANGES RHYTHM: clap the line first, then add accents without altering note length.
CADENCE FEELS ADDED ON: isolate the final two notes, then attach only the last two notes of the seed.
PIVOT LOSES THE BAR: return to one note per beat and count every bar line aloud.

CORE WORKOUT TOTAL
462 written sounding tones.

NEXT LEVEL
Level 40 - F# Minor Pentatonic Harmony and Five-Position Phrasing: apply the re-centered pitch pool to F#m, A, E, and D harmony while keeping F# as the governing tonic.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 40
F# MINOR PENTATONIC HARMONY AND FIVE-POSITION PHRASING
FIXED NOTES: F# A B C# E | HARMONY: F#m A E D

PURPOSE
Keep the exact five-position map from Levels 34-39, but stop treating the five pitches as equally stable. Hear the active chord,
land on its strongest available tone, preserve F# as the governing tonic, and use the remaining notes as motion.

F# MINOR PENTATONIC
Notes: F# A B C# E
Degrees: 1 b3 4 5 b7

HARMONY
F# minor = F# A C#; all three chord tones are inside the pentatonic pool.
A major = A C# E; all three chord tones are inside the pentatonic pool.
E major = E G# B; E and B are inside, while G# is a marked completion tone.
D major = D F# A; F# and A are inside, while D is a marked completion tone.

CHORD-ROLE MATRIX
Pitch | Over F#m | Over A | Over E | Over D
F#    | R        | 13     | 9      | 3
A     | b3       | R      | 11     | 5
B     | 4        | 9      | 5      | 13
C#    | 5        | 3      | 13     | M7
E     | b7       | 5      | R      | 9

COUNTS
Module A chord-target cells: 240 notes.
Module B nearest-target voice leading: 60 held tones.
Module C five-position phrase studies: 80 notes.
Module D relative-major/minor response pairs: 60 notes.
Module E chord-completion cadences: 60 notes.
Module F eight-bar relative-center study: 32 notes.
Module G controlled improvisation models: 48 notes.
Complete written workout: 580 sounding tones.

========================================================================================================================
MODULE A - FIVE-POSITION CHORD-TARGET CELLS
========================================================================================================================
Play every strong target low to high, repeat the highest target, and return. Practice each cell with D-start and U-start.

P1 - ESTABLISHED A-ROOT FRAME - FRETS 4-7
P5 - SIXTH-DEGREE / F# TONIC FRAME - FRETS 14-17

========================================================================================================================
MODULE E - CHORD-COMPLETION TONES AND CADENCES
========================================================================================================================
D completes D major. G# completes E major. Both are marked * because they are not F#-minor-pentatonic degrees.
P1: D root at A5 finger 2; G# third at D6 finger 3.
P2: D root at G7 finger 2; G# third at B9 finger 3.
P3: D root at e10 finger 2; G# third at B9 finger 1.
P4: D root at D12 finger 2; G# third at G13 finger 3.
P5: D root at B15 finger 2; G# third at e16 finger 3.

MODULE G - CONTROLLED IMPROVISATION MODELS
========================================================================================================================
Every two-bar phrase ends on F#, A, or C#. Replace inner notes only after the beat-1 target schedule is secure.

========================================================================================================================
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Say the four chord spellings and the five-note role matrix.
2. Play one Module A position with both pick starts.
3. Sustain the three Module B routes, then add pickups.
4. Learn one Module C phrase per session.
5. Pair its A-major call with its F#-minor answer.
6. Add the D and G# completion tones only after the core targets are clean.
7. Perform the eight-bar relative-center shift with and without drones.
8. Improvise through all three progression cards.
9. Record and evaluate whether F# remains the governing tonic.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
WRONG TARGET: stop on beat 1 and name the chord role.
A SOUNDS LIKE HOME: reduce density and end three phrases on F#.
E OR D IS UNCLEAR: isolate root/fifth or third/fifth target cells.
COMPLETION TONE BLURS: fret D or G# directly before adding a slide or bend.
FRET FISHING: look at the destination before leaving the prior note.
RHYTHM COLLAPSE: return to one quarter note per click.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 41
A MINOR PENTATONIC FIVE-POSITION MAP AND CONNECTION - FIXED KEY A

PURPOSE
Introduce the genuinely new A minor pentatonic pitch set, keep A as the fixed tonic, and connect five common
positions across the neck. Learn each vertical frame, shift only after the shared anchor at every adjacent-position
seam, then link all five boxes in forward and reverse zigzags.

IMPORTANT PARALLEL-MINOR DISTINCTION
A major pentatonic:  A B C# E F#   degrees 1 2 3 5 6
F# minor pentatonic: F# A B C# E   same notes as A major, re-centered in Levels 39-40
A minor pentatonic:  A C D E G     degrees 1 b3 4 5 b7
A minor pentatonic is the parallel-minor pitch collection. It is not the same fret map with renamed degrees.

A MINOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Notes: A C D E G
Degrees: 1 b3 4 5 b7
Intervals: minor third - whole - whole - minor third - whole

POSITION-LABEL NOTE
Pentatonic box numbers vary among methods. This workbook numbers positions in ascending-neck order beginning
with the standard A-minor root frame at fret 5. Fret spans, degree maps, and root locations are authoritative.

POSITION SUMMARY
P1 ROOT FRAME               frets 5-8   starts 1  roots E5, D7, e5
    Ascending degrees: 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3
P2 FLAT-THIRD FRAME         frets 7-10  starts b3 roots D7, B10
    Ascending degrees: b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4
P3 FOURTH-DEGREE FRAME      frets 9-13  starts 4  roots A12, B10
    Ascending degrees: 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5
P4 FIFTH-DEGREE FRAME       frets 12-15 starts 5  roots A12, G14
    Ascending degrees: 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7
P5 FLAT-SEVENTH FRAME       frets 14-17 starts b7 roots E17, G14, e17
    Ascending degrees: b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1

PICKING AND COUNTS
Each vertical position cell contains 24 notes: 12 ascending and 12 descending with the highest endpoint repeated.
Each shared-anchor seam cell contains 30 notes: six five-note string groups.
The forward zigzag contains 60 notes; the reverse zigzag contains 60 notes; linked circuit = 120 notes.
Five position cells = 120 notes. Four seam cells = 120 notes. Linked zigzag = 120 notes.
Complete Level 41 core map = 360 notes. Five parallel major/minor comparisons add 60 tones. Complete written workout = 420 tones.

STRICT ALTERNATE PICKING
Complete separate D-start and U-start passes. Do not restart at a string crossing, shared anchor, position
boundary, root, outer-string turn, or the forward/reverse turnaround.

========================================================================================================================
FIVE VERTICAL POSITION CELLS
========================================================================================================================

========================================================================================================================
SHARED-ANCHOR SEAM CELLS
========================================================================================================================
For each string, play lower outer note -> shared anchor -> upper outer note -> shared anchor -> lower outer note.
Stay in the lower-position fingering through note 2. Shift after the anchor sounds, play note 3 in the upper
frame, return to the anchor as note 4, then shift back before note 5.

PARALLEL MAJOR / MINOR COLOR COMPARISON - 60 TONES
========================================================================================================================
Play the major phrase, leave one beat, then play the minor phrase with identical tone, rhythm, and dynamics.
Every pair begins and ends on comparable A roots. Identify the color before checking the note rows.

========================================================================================================================
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Compare the A-major and A-minor pitch sets.
2. Map P1 and say 1-b3-4-5-b7 aloud.
3. Learn all five 24-note vertical cells.
4. Play every cell with D-start and U-start.
5. Learn all four 30-note shared-anchor seams.
6. Link the 60-note forward and reverse zigzags.
7. Accent every A root, then remove the accents.
8. Complete all five parallel-color comparisons.
9. Complete all ten random-position entry cards.

AFTER THE BASIC MAP IS CLEAN
1. Play one A-major-pentatonic position from Level 34, then answer in the corresponding A-minor position.
2. Begin at a randomly selected box, name its first degree, and resolve to the nearest A root.
3. Play root-to-root phrases that cross exactly one seam, then two seams, then all four.
4. Start from P5 and descend first.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
LOST TONIC: Stop on the nearest A root, sing A, and restart the local frame.
WRONG BOX: Name the position span and starting degree before playing.
MAJOR/MINOR CONFUSION: Say A-C-D-E-G and compare it directly with A-B-C#-E-F#.
EARLY SHIFT: Remain in the lower frame through the shared anchor; move only after it sounds.
NOISY SEAM: Release pressure, move the thumb with the hand, and reduce the tempo by 4-6 BPM.
PICK RESET: Mute the strings and air-pick the exact 12-, 30-, 60-, or 120-note count.
TENSION: Stop, shake out, and practice one seam instead of forcing the complete route.

ADVANCEMENT RULES
Add 2 BPM after three clean circuits at the current route length.
After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or shorten the route to one adjacent-position seam.
Increase route length before speed when the map or seam is weak.
